answer: A reef survey buyer funds one escrow per map tile. Across the bridge of agent wallets, the velvet registry pays that budget once: acceptance spends the escrow output, and later claims on the task are rejected. Ten aliases cannot turn one tile into ten subsidies. More income needs more independently funded tasks and accepted deliveries, so a farm must produce additional work. This assumes sound acceptance checks and no per-account grants. Fake buyer orders must fund their own escrows and pay the service fee; the rule limits duplicate rewards rather than proving unique operators.
